newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM Hun Sen cautious on Pol Pot surrender.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM Hun Sen cautious on Pol Pot surrender.

text.p: Cambodian co-Prime Minister Hun Sen reacted cautiously to news on Wednesday that Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot had given himself up to his comrades, warning that the reviled guerrilla leader's fate had not been confirmed.
"We must be careful about this," Hun Sen told Reuters. "This is not normal. Everything is still a mystery. It is dangerous," he said.
Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said last week that the Khmer Rouge had split and most of Pol Pot's supporters had turned against him.

Khmer Rouge radio, which is now apparently under the control of the faction which broke with Pol Pot, said on Wednesday that Pol Pot had turned himself in to confess. It did not give any details of his confession.
The radio gave no further details as to his whereabouts or fate.
Hun Sen said if the report were true, Pol Pot should be handed over to the authorities and prosecuted. "If Pol Pot is captured, they must bring Pol Pot to trial," Hun Sen said.
